notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

PS2 sound: some consoles lost all PS2 sound after switching between the two PS2 engines, on both engines from then on. The console's sound system remembers a volume, a mute and an output for each app, and both PS2 engines go by one name, so one bad memory silenced both. Games now start without that memory, at full volume on the output in use.

Sound follows the output: when the console switches between the speaker, the TV, headphones and Bluetooth, playing sound now follows the switch without being tied to the old output. Before, a game could reopen on the output it used last time, for example the speaker while docked.

Deep sleep: the line under Deep sleep in Settings now covers everything since you last used the console: how long, the battery used, how often it woke by itself (charger or USB-C) and how long it stayed awake with the screen off, and why. Sleeping in a game, a wake nobody pressed now goes straight back to sleep; before, the game went on running, sound included, behind the dark screen.

Set a Custom RAM Setting: when Test it cannot start, its message now shows under the button. It used to appear at the bottom of the page, out of sight, so the button seemed to do nothing.

PC game uploads from the web page: the page no longer reloads itself while a PC game is uploading, which hid the upload and its Try again. Sending a game to the SD card again after a stopped upload no longer fails every retry with "did not arrive complete".

3DS saves on the web page show the game's name even when the game is not on the console, and for compressed 3DS games too.

The debug report has a section on USB file transfer, for when a computer does not see the console.

New and lightly tested: the deep sleep change was not tried with a real wake by the charger, and the sound change was not tried docked.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
